Hoarding Cleanouts Handled With Respect, Anywhere in Toronto

c: Cleaning out a hoarder’s house is rarely a simple job, and it’s almost never a simple decision to make either. Live Junk Free has spent years doing hoarding cleanouts across Toronto — semis and rows in Riverdale and Roncesvalles with narrow stairwells and tight laneways, condo suites downtown where a situation has built up quietly behind a closed door, postwar bungalows in Etobicoke and Scarborough where a family member has lived alone for years. Whatever the address, the approach stays the same: no commentary, no judgment, a steady room-by-room pace, and a crew that treats the person and the property with the same respect they’d want for their own family. The 700+ five-star reviews behind Live Junk Free come from families, executors, landlords and individuals themselves — people who needed a hoarding cleanout done properly, quietly, and without anyone feeling like a spectacle.

blocks.text: WHY CHOOSE OUR HOARDING CLEANOUT SERVICE
What Sets Live Junk Free's Hoarding Cleanouts Apart in Toronto

items.title: Judgment-free hoarding cleanouts, every single time
text: There’s no commentary, no reaction, and no assumption made about how a home reached the state it’s in. The crew’s job is to clear it carefully and respectfully — not to comment on it.

items.title: Discreet, unmarked scheduling on request
text: Arrival times can be arranged for quieter hours, vehicles can be unmarked, and nothing about the visit needs to be visible to neighbours or the street. Privacy is treated as the default, not a special request.

items.title: A pace that respects the person living in the space
text: Hoarding cleanouts move at whatever speed actually works — some households need one visit, others need several sessions spread over weeks. The resident’s own priorities and comfort guide the schedule wherever that’s possible.

items.title: Coordination with family, executors and support workers
text: Adult children, social workers, property managers and healthcare professionals are often part of a hoarding cleanout, and Live Junk Free works alongside all of them — updates, documentation and photographs provided as needed, without the family having to manage every detail themselves.

items.title: Donation-first sorting, not a straight haul to landfill
text: Furniture, clothing and household goods with life left in them go to donation partners first. Only what’s genuinely unusable goes to disposal, and metals and electronics are routed to licensed recyclers.

items.title: Free on-site quotes, with an honest cost to clean out a hoarder's house
text: A crew member walks the property, sees the real scope, and gives one flat number before anything moves — no guessing based on a phone description, and no surprise costs once work is underway.

blocks.text: HOARDING CLEANOUT FAQ
Hoarding Cleanouts in Toronto — Honest Answers to Common Questions

items.q: What's the cost to clean out a hoarder's house?
a: Hoarder clean out cost depends on the volume of belongings, the number of rooms affected, and how much sorting and donation coordination is needed — a single room is a modest job, a full multi-floor property costs more given the time involved. The exact figure is confirmed free at a private walkthrough, with no obligation to proceed.

items.q: What's the best way to clean out a hoarder's house?
a: Professional help, a clear plan, and patience — going in with a truck and no strategy usually causes more distress than progress. The most effective approach sorts systematically (keep, donate, recycle, dispose), respects the resident’s input wherever they’re able to give it, and moves at a pace the household can actually handle, sometimes across more than one visit. Safety concerns — structural issues, pest infestations, mould — get identified and handled by the right specialists before the rest of the cleanout continues.

Completely. No commentary is made about how a space reached its current state, no photos are taken beyond what’s needed for the quote or documentation requested, and the crew’s entire focus is on clearing the space carefully and respectfully.

items.q: Can the cleanout happen while the person continues living in the home?
a: Yes, and this is one of the most common ways a hoarding cleanout in Toronto actually happens. Work can proceed room by room while the resident stays in the home throughout, at a pace that keeps the space livable at every stage rather than displacing anyone.

items.q: What happens if we find valuables, documents or sentimental items?
a: They’re set aside immediately and brought to the family or the resident, never sorted into a donation or disposal pile by default. This applies to cash, jewellery, important paperwork and anything that looks meaningful, without exception.
